title: Operation Midnight Ledger: ransomware tabletop exercise
scenario: A mid-sized organization (about 400 staff, hybrid cloud, Microsoft 365 and on-premises file servers) is hit by a ransomware affiliate that entered through a phished contractor account. The exercise runs from first alert to recovery and lessons learned.
objectives: Validate escalation from the SOC to the incident commander and executives
Exercise containment decisions under time pressure and incomplete information
Test legal, regulatory and customer notification decision-making
Confirm backups can be trusted and restoration order is agreed
Identify gaps in the incident response plan, contact lists and tooling

injects.text: Monday 06:40. EDR alerts on a contractor laptop: encoded PowerShell launched from an Office document, then outbound HTTPS to an unfamiliar domain every 60 seconds.
injects.question: Who is notified, and what are the first three actions?

injects.text: Sign-in logs show the contractor account authenticated from two countries 20 minutes apart. The account was added to a privileged group at 03:12. Domain controller logs show an LSASS memory access event.
injects.question: What is the scope now, and does this change severity?

injects.text: File servers FS-01 and FS-02 begin renaming files with a .lockd extension. A ransom note demands 40 BTC within 72 hours and claims 300 GB of HR and finance data was stolen.
injects.question: Do you disconnect the network? What do you keep running?

injects.text: A reporter emails Communications asking for comment on 'a cyberattack at your company'. Staff are posting on social media that systems are down.
injects.question: What is said externally and internally, and who approves it?

injects.text: Forensics confirms data was staged and exfiltrated to cloud storage. The HR share contained names, SSNs and bank details for 2,100 employees. Cyber insurance requires notice within 24 hours.
injects.question: What notification obligations apply, and when does each clock start?

injects.text: The executive sponsor asks: 'Should we just pay? How long will restoring from backup take?' Backups are immutable but the last full restore test was 14 months ago.
injects.question: How is the payment decision made, and what information does leadership need?

injects.text: Clean backups are verified. IT proposes restoring all servers at once to get back online fastest.
injects.question: What is the restoration order and how do you prevent reinfection?

injects.text: Operations are restored. The board wants to know what happened, what it cost and what will change.
injects.question: What goes in the after-action report and who owns each improvement?
